references.text: Psalm 68:2 contains almost identical wording: 'God arises, his enemies are scattered, those who hate him flee before his face.' This is a direct parallel to Moses' prayer at the departure of the ark.
Psalm 132:8 refers to the ark rising and going to its resting place, linking it to the same theme of the ark's movement and the Lord's presence.
The description of the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat where the Lord meets Moses provides background for why the ark represents God's presence when it sets out.
The ark goes before the people across the Jordan, showing its role as leader of Israel's journey, as in Numbers 10:35.
The ark is carried out to war against the Philistines, demonstrating faith that the Lord's presence in the ark would scatter the enemies.
Solomon quotes similar words at the dedication of the temple: 'Arise, O Lord God, go to your resting place.' This connects directly to Moses' prayer.
A contrasting example where the ark does not go with the people into battle, and the enemies do not flee, but Israel is defeated - showing the significance of the ark.
Moses' blessing over Levi mentions the Lord's enemies and those who hate him, using similar language.
